precepts.text: To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light: from sin to righteousness. And from the power of Satan unto God: from the prince of the power of the air, his evil communication, those unclean spirits out of the mouth of the dragon, the beast, and the false prophet.
precepts.point: Even as Sodom and Gomorrha, giving themselves over to fornication, and going after strange flesh: other nations, and worse, as it is today. They are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire: that lake of fire we read about in Revelation 14.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
Christ sent Paul, “Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee, To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light”. To open our eyes, and turn us from darkness to light: from sin to righteousness.

Then, “and from the power of Satan unto God”: from the power of Satan, the prince of the power of the air, his evil communication, those unclean spirits that went out of the mouth of the dragon, the beast and the false prophet. So “that they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.”

That is the other side of Jude. Some are bound in chains of darkness, loving darkness rather than light, ordained of old to that condemnation. But the ones Paul was sent to are turned from darkness to light and from Satan unto God, sanctified by faith in Christ. That is the faith once delivered unto the saints that we are earnestly contending for, casting down Esau's lies about fallen angels and Nephilim.

precepts.text: Paul shut up the saints in prison, gave his voice against them when they were put to death, punished them in every synagogue and compelled them to blaspheme, exceedingly mad against them even unto strange cities: what he did the Pharisees and later the inquisitors under Ferdinand and Isabella all did, and it is what Christ said denying him under persecution looks like. Some here are hirelings who will fold.
precepts.point: The hairs of your head are numbered and you are of more value than sparrows. Whosoever confesses me before men under tribulation I will confess, and whosoever denies me under torture, my husband forced me, I never believed it, I will deny.

note.label: From Exile & Tribulation to Promise

precepts.why:
Christ says, “But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.” Under what conditions? Not at work saying, yeah, I believe in God. Read in context, it is tribulation, persecution, Jacob's trouble: I never believed that Israelite stuff, I don't believe in those commandments, my husband forced me, my wife forced me.

Paul testified what denying looks like from the persecutor's side: “Which thing I also did in Jerusalem: and many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them.”

“And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme”. Compel means he forced them to blaspheme. That is what Christ was talking about: deny me under torture, persecution, tribulation, hard times. That is the trial all of us alive at this time must go through.

Paul was not the only persecutor. What Paul did, they were all doing: the Pharisees, and later the inquisitors under Queen Isabella and King Ferdinand in the time of Spain and Portugal, whose job was to hunt down Israelites keeping the commandments, to Africa, to Mexico, to South and North America.

And “being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.” That is why Christ said, when they persecute you in this city, flee into another.

Everybody in here says they love God, but some of us are liars. Some are not valiant for the truth; you are a professional student, a hireling. The hireling sees the wolf coming and leaves the sheep. Think about being compelled to blaspheme, as in the film Unthinkable, where they brought in a man's wife and kids to make him confess. You think that could never happen to you; the devil is a liar. What Paul was doing is what Christ said is going to happen.

precepts.text: Paul witnessed none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come. The law and the prophets were his source material.
precepts.point: Beware lest ye also, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own steadfastness. The error of the wicked says all nations can be saved, Paul grafted the nations in, adultery is permitted, the Sabbath changed, and the laws are done away. Grow in grace and in the knowledge of our Lord.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

precepts.why:
Peter says Paul wrote “according to the wisdom given unto him”, and wisdom is not a what but a who: Christ is the wisdom given to Paul. And Peter read “all his epistles”. He didn't say, this is off but I'll let it slide. If Paul wrote things that were off, that implicates Peter; if it implicates Peter it implicates James; and it implicates John, the last surviving disciple, who never wrote against Paul. You make Christ a negligent Messiah who sat quiet while Paul wrote error and then waited three thousand years to send somebody to fix it.

So what did Paul write from? “Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come”. When Paul crafted his letters, his primary reference was none other than what the prophets and Moses wrote. That is Paul's source material.

That is why Peter says the unlearned and unstable wrest Paul “as they do also the other scriptures”: the law and the prophets. Wrest is short for wrestle; they twist Paul into saying what he did not say, because they don't really believe what the Bible says. The error of the wicked takes Paul's letters and says all nations can be saved, Paul grafted the nations in, we can commit adultery, the Sabbath is changed, we don't have to keep the laws anymore. Don't fall from your own stedfastness: Paul said none other things than Moses and the prophets.

precepts.text: Witnessing both to small and great, saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come. Acts 28:23: persuading them concerning Jesus out of the law of Moses and out of the prophets. Paul's letters are 99.9 percent law and prophets; the rest, like the unbelieving wife departing, is the wisdom given him for that time, because under Moses she got death.
precepts.point: Beware lest ye, being led away with the error of the wicked, fall from your own steadfastness. The error comes from those who stumble at the other scriptures, the Old Testament. When you teach your oppressor can receive the same benefits as you, that the nations receive some twisted salvation, you are in the error of the wicked.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

precepts.why:
What was Paul's source material? “Having therefore obtained help of God, I continue unto this day, witnessing both to small and great”, leaders and students, teachers and students, “saying none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come”. Paul only taught what Moses and the prophets said.

And in Acts 28, when many came to his lodging, he “expounded and testified the kingdom of God, persuading them concerning Jesus, both out of the law of Moses, and out of the prophets, from morning till evening.” His letters are based on the law and the prophets. He was not sitting around making things up.

That is why Peter mentions “the other scriptures”: to understand Paul's letters you must understand the other scriptures. Are there places where the spirit of Christ spoke through Paul and things were added? Yes. Paul's letters are 99.9 percent law and prophets, and maybe one percent is something like the unbelieving wife departing, which is not found in Moses, because under Moses, if she did not believe, she got death. Your wife could believe in Satan in the wilderness and she got death. That was added for that time, and that is “the wisdom given unto him”: Christ speaking through Paul.

When people don't study Paul, they say Paul's letters aren't authoritative, Mark and Luke weren't of the twelve, and they begin to speak evil of dignities. Then the Lord blinds their minds, and Satan has them teaching that nations can be saved. We have been thoroughbreds in Paul's letters since learning Acts 10 and Romans 11 at the Bishop's house in 2006.

precepts.text: That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead. He is the firstborn of death.
precepts.point: The gin shall take him by the heel, terrors shall make him afraid on every side, the missiles, and the firstborn of death shall devour his strength; Acts 26:23 says Christ is the first that should rise from the dead. He is brought to the king of terrors, brimstone is scattered on his habitation, his branch, his children, is cut off, his remembrance perishes from the earth, and he is driven from light into darkness and chased out of the world. Knowing Esau will be like a bad dream. Such are the dwellings of the wicked, him that knoweth not God.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

precepts.why:
“Terrors shall make him afraid on every side”: the missiles, the ICBMs. “His strength shall be hungerbitten, and destruction shall be ready at his side. It shall devour the strength of his skin: even the firstborn of death shall devour his strength.”

Who is the firstborn of death? Paul tells it: “That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead”. That is the firstborn of death right there: Christ. He was the first raised up.

So it is Christ who will devour Esau's strength. “His confidence shall be rooted out of his tabernacle, and it shall bring him to the king of terrors.” Your slave master, the one who taught you how to fear God, will be brought to the king of terrors. “brimstone shall be scattered upon his habitation. His roots shall be dried up beneath, and above shall his branch be cut off.” His branch is his children. The one who rose first from the dead is the one who cuts him off.

precepts.text: You hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins.
precepts.point: A sister leaving her husband to stay with a mother or aunt in the world is Satan's chess move. Seek believers who can build you up.

note.label: Pattern

precepts.why:
Christ sent Paul “To open their eyes, and to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins”. These are the people we are fighting for. Our job is to open the eyes of our people and bring them back to the light, to the commandments, and to the knowledge of who God is: Christ is a black man, he died only for the nation of Israel, and he will return for Israel alone.

Our people are in a state of darkness, and Paul says what that state is: “And you hath he quickened, who were dead in trespasses and sins; Wherein in time past ye walked according to the course of this world”. Our people are dead because they destroyed themselves by breaking God's commandments. They are in a state of death, without conscience, bound by Satan. Whatever the world offers, that is what they follow after.

So when you look at your mother, your uncle, your auntie inside these religions, they are bound by Satan. That is why a sister who separates from her husband and goes to her mother's house, her aunt's house or a friend's house in the world is making Satan's move. What is your mom going to teach you? She is not awake out of this dark place. Leaving a sister in the truth to live with an aunt in the world is a good chess move by Satan, and if you're not wise you won't catch it. Go to the believers who can guide you, teach you and build you up.

Will Smith reached the end of money and fame and found it could not make him happy: a man in pain, crying for help, whose soul is damaged. That is the course of this world. The dead must be quickened, and the pattern to follow is the fruit of the Spirit, meditating in the word, fasting and praying, and examining yourselves whether ye be in the faith.

precepts.point: This is the same hope Paul taught. Paul's mission was to go teach the twelve tribes of Israel, to show the Jews there is no more animal sacrifice and to show the Gentiles they must come back and keep God's laws for hope's sake. Our hope comes from the patience and comfort of the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 130: Israel, Hope in the Lord

precepts.why: “Let Israel hope in the Lord”. This is the same hope Paul taught. He begins with himself: “My manner of life from my youth, which was at the first among mine own nation at Jerusalem, know all the Jews”. Paul’s manner of life from his youth was known among his own nation at Jerusalem; he was of Israel, the people who have this hope.

Paul's mission was to go teach the twelve tribes of Israel, to show the Jews there is no more animal sacrifice and to show the Gentiles they must come back and keep God's laws for hope's sake. Our hope comes from the patience and comfort of the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 130: Israel, Hope in the Lord

precepts.why: The Jews “knew me from the beginning, if they would testify, that after the most straitest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.” Paul lived a Pharisee after the most straitest sect of the religion, and his mission was to go teach the twelve tribes of Israel: to show the Jews there is no more animal sacrifice and to show the Gentiles they must come back and keep God’s laws for hope’s sake.

Our hope comes from the patience and comfort of the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 130: Israel, Hope in the Lord

precepts.why: “And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers”. Paul stands for the hope of the promise made to the fathers. That is the hope of Israel: mercy with the Most High, and with him plenteous redemption.

precepts.text: Unto which promise the twelve tribes, serving God day and night, hope to come.
precepts.point: This is the same hope Paul taught. Paul's mission was to go teach the twelve tribes of Israel, to show the Jews there is no more animal sacrifice and to show the Gentiles they must come back and keep God's laws for hope's sake. Our hope comes from the patience and comfort of the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 130: Israel, Hope in the Lord

precepts.why: “Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come. For which hope’s sake, king Agrippa, I am accused of the Jews.” The hope belongs to the twelve tribes serving God day and night. Only the people of Israel, the so-called blacks, Spanish, and native Indians, can have this hope of repentance and eternal life, and it is the very hope Paul was accused for.

precepts.text: That they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.
precepts.point: The fruits meet for repentance are works, not offerings brought to cover sin.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
When John saw the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism he called them a generation of vipers and told them, “Bring forth therefore fruits meet for repentance”. Paul preached the same thing, to Damascus, Jerusalem, all the coasts of Judea and then to the Gentiles: “that they should repent and turn to God, and do works meet for repentance.”

The fruits meet for repentance are works. Repentance is turning to God and doing works, not offerings brought to cover sin. That is what John demanded of the Pharisees and Sadducees, and what Paul preached everywhere he went.

precepts.text: None other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come, that Christ should suffer.
precepts.point: What he came to fulfil is the prophecies written concerning him, not the commandments given to Israel to keep. Everything in chapter 2 of this same gospel is an example of that fulfilling.

note.label: Matthew 5: The Sermon on the Mount and the Magnifying of the Law

precepts.why:
Paul, standing before Agrippa, said he witnessed “none other things than those which the prophets and Moses did say should come: That Christ should suffer, and that he should be the first that should rise from the dead, and should shew light unto the people, and to the Gentiles.”

Moses and the prophets said Christ should suffer and rise. That is what Christ came to fulfil: what was said should come concerning him. Paul preached nothing else. None of it is the doing away of the commandments; it is the bringing to pass of what was foretold.

precepts.text: Paul says to Agrippa, I know thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews.
precepts.point: John had told Herod plainly, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother's wife. Herod knew the law well enough to be accused by it, because those rulers were schooled in the customs of Israel.

note.label: Mark 6: A Prophet Without Honour, the Death of John, and the Five Thousand

precepts.why:
Herod hears of Christ and says, “It is John, whom I beheaded: he is risen from the dead.” He had bound John in prison for Herodias' sake, his brother Philip's wife, “For John had said unto Herod, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother’s wife.”

John told him plainly it was not lawful, and Herod knew the law well enough to be accused by it. Those rulers were schooled in the customs of Israel. Paul says as much to Agrippa: “Especially because I know thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.” Agrippa was expert in all the customs and questions among the Jews, and Herod was no different. He was not ignorant of the law he broke; he knew it, took his brother's wife anyway, and then took John's head.

precepts.text: Paul stands judged for the hope of the promise made unto the fathers, unto which the twelve tribes hope to come; his ministry was to Israel.
precepts.point: The promise is unto you and to your children and to all that are afar off, meaning Israel and their seed, not all races and nations. The "afar off" are the scattered ones of verse 5, the Israelites dispersed to the four corners of the earth, as many as the Most High shall call.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
Before Agrippa, Paul says he is judged “for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers: Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come.”

The promise was made to the fathers, and the twelve tribes are the ones hoping to come to it. Paul's ministry was to Israel. The all that are afar off in Peter's words are those twelve tribes, the scattered ones of verse 5, dispersed to the four corners of the earth.

precepts.text: Paul's own confession: he shut up the saints in prison, gave his voice against them when put to death, punished them in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme.
precepts.point: This is the true meaning of loving your enemies. Christianity twists it to mean love the ones who enslaved, raped, and colonized your ancestors, stole your nationality, land, and heritage, miseducated you, gave you a false image of God, and today shut down anyone who says Israel is the true children of God. That is not the enemy the scripture means. The Bible means love the enemies within your own nation, because Paul, who persecuted and killed the disciples, was one of those enemies who could still repent.

note.label: Acts 9: A Chosen Vessel

precepts.why:
Paul's own confession of what Ananias had heard by many: “many of the saints did I shut up in prison, having received authority from the chief priests; and when they were put to death, I gave my voice against them. And I punished them oft in every synagogue, and compelled them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly mad against them, I persecuted them even unto strange cities.”

He shut up the saints in prison, gave his voice against them when they were put to death, punished them in every synagogue and compelled them to blaspheme, chasing them from city to city with zeal. Ananias was right about the man, and still that man repented. The things we all did in the world were worthy of death, so who are we to say a man is beyond repentance?

precepts.text: The promise made of God unto the fathers is the hope of the twelve tribes, not of every nation.
precepts.point: The purpose is that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles, the northern tribes, through Christ, who redeemed the twelve tribes from the curse of the law given to Israel. "All nations blessed in Abraham" means the tribes within Abraham's seed, not every nation on earth.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

precepts.why:
“And now I stand and am judged for the hope of the promise made of God unto our fathers: Unto which promise our twelve tribes, instantly serving God day and night, hope to come.”

The promise made of God unto the fathers is the hope of the twelve tribes, not of every nation. That promise, remission of sins through his name, is what Peter preached in Cornelius' house.

precepts.text: Agrippa tells Paul, "Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian," meaning a follower of the anointed one.
precepts.point: The disciples were called Christians first in Antioch, and those disciples were Jews. Christians were not all nations or races as men think today; the Greek word Christianos comes from Christos, the anointed one, so a Christian is a kinsman of the Messiah and a follower of Christ, an anointed one.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“And the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch.” Those disciples were Jews. Christians were not all nations or races as men think today. The Greek word Christianos comes from Christos, the anointed one, so a Christian is a kinsman of the Messiah and a follower of Christ, an anointed one.

“Then Agrippa said unto Paul, Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian.” Agrippa meant a follower of the anointed one. That is what the name meant when it was first given at Antioch.

precepts.why: Paul was on trial before Herod Agrippa II. This proves that these guys were converts. “I think myself happy, king Agrippa, because I shall answer for myself this day before thee touching all the things whereof I am accused of the Jews: Especially because I know thee to be expert in all customs and questions which are among the Jews: wherefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.” You see that: they were well learned in all the customs of the Jews. These were converts, these were Edomite converts. Acts 13:1 shows how they became expert.
